name: Haiku
summary: Free and open-source desktop operating system inspired by BeOS, equipped with a modular preemptive hybrid kernel, the indexed BFS file system and the Deskbar/Tracker desktop environment.
license: Open Source (MIT Licence with BeOS OpenTracker components)

content.introduction: Haiku is a free and open-source operating system designed specifically for personal desktop computing and multimedia creation. Founded in 2001 under the initial name OpenBeOS following the commercial abandonment of BeOS by Palm Inc., the project offers a complete, modern and independent reimplementation of the technologies of BeOS R5. Without being based on Linux or on classic Unix, Haiku offers a unified user experience, particularly lightweight, fast and centred on graphical responsiveness.
content.what_is_it: Technically, Haiku is a stand-alone operating system developed from scratch (with the exception of Tracker and Deskbar released by Be Inc. in 2001). It combines a modular preemptive hybrid kernel, a journalled file system with metadata indexed in a database (BFS), a highly responsive spatial graphical interface and an object-oriented C++ API organised in logical kits, offering binary compatibility with the historical software of BeOS on 32-bit architecture and source code compatibility on 64-bit architecture.
content.kernel_architecture_and_newos: The heart of Haiku is a modular preemptive hybrid kernel derived from the NewOS kernel, developed by Travis Geiselbrecht (a former engineer at Be Inc.). The kernel ensures granular preemptive multitasking, virtual memory protection, dynamic loading of hardware driver modules and complete support for symmetric multiprocessing (SMP) on multi-core processors. The architecture imposes intensive multithreading: each application window has by default its own execution and graphical rendering threads, preventing the interface from freezing when a task consumes computing cycles.
content.file_system_bfs_and_live_queries: The cornerstone of the data organisation of Haiku is the 64-bit journalled file system **BFS** (Be File System), originally designed by Dominic Giampaolo. BFS treats files as structured records: any file can integrate arbitrary typed metadata (for example artist, album and bitrate for a music file; status and deadline for a project), which are automatically indexed by the system. Users can formulate persistent dynamic queries (live queries) that update in real time in the form of virtual folders as soon as files matching the criteria are created or modified.
content.deskbar_tracker_and_object_oriented_api: The visual environment of Haiku forms an indivisible and elegant whole. The **Deskbar** (modular taskbar lodged by default in the top right corner) gives access to applications, applets and volume control. The spatial **Tracker** file manager makes it possible to browse through disks and display files in the form of customised attribute tables. The windowing system integrates the innovative *Stack & Tile* technology, making it possible to group and stack several windows as tabs within a single frame. For developers, the Haiku C++ API is structured in modular kits (Application, Interface, Storage, Media, Network), guaranteeing object programming of great clarity.
content.modern_features_and_hardware_support: While preserving the spirit of BeOS, Haiku has equipped itself with contemporary advances: an innovative package management system (`HaikuPackage`) which mounts software as read-only virtual file systems (`.hpkg`) in `/system` without scattering files on the disk, a modern web browser based on WebKit (WebPositive), and Wi-Fi and network drivers ported from the FreeBSD kernel. Haiku is available in a 32-bit edition (with dual gcc2/gcc13 compiler for binary compatibility with the BeOS software of the period) and in a 64-bit edition (modern x86-64 for UEFI PCs).
content.release_status_and_installation_media: At the time of consultation the current release was R1/beta6, dated 26 August 2026, on two supported platforms: x86 in 32-bit and 64-bit builds. The published images can be written to a USB flash drive, an empty disk or DVD media, and are usable in two ways: booted live from the medium without installing, or used to install Haiku to a disk or partition. The same images run in QEMU, VMware or VirtualBox. Distribution relies on a set of donated mirrors, and each release is published with SHA256 checksums and torrent files; upgrade instructions are provided separately for installations of an earlier version.
advantages: Operating system entirely dedicated to the personal workstation, offering exceptional user interface responsiveness.
Native multi-threaded architecture preventing the interface from freezing during heavy computations or input/output operations.
Remarkable BFS file system with indexed metadata and dynamic real-time search queries (live queries).
Advanced ergonomic features such as *Stack & Tile* to organise and group application windows as tabs.
Modern non-destructive `.hpkg` package system based on the mounting of read-only virtual file systems.
Free permissive MIT licence and binary compatibility preserved with the historical software of BeOS R5 in the 32-bit version.
disadvantages: Application catalogue smaller than that of the major general-purpose systems (Linux, Windows, macOS), despite the porting of major software.
Compatibility with very recent computer hardware (notably hardware 3D acceleration of modern GPUs and latest-generation Wi-Fi) still partial.
The system is still officially in the pre-1.0 development phase (successive beta versions), and can show occasional instabilities.
Absence of a partitioned multi-user system with strict access rights (the system is designed for a single user on their personal machine).
Not suited to enterprise server deployments without a screen or to cloud-type container infrastructures.
who_is_it_for: Nostalgics and enthusiasts of the BeOS environment wishing to find again its elegance, its speed and its unique ergonomics.
Users looking for an extremely lightweight, responsive and refined personal desktop system for office work and web consultation.
C++ developers appreciating the clarity and elegance of a unified object-oriented API organised in coherent software kits.
The curious and enthusiasts of alternative architectures wanting to explore a mature non-Unix and non-Windows operating system.
who_is_it_not_for: Professionals depending on closed commercial software suites (Adobe Creative Cloud, Autodesk, Microsoft Office).
Players of modern PC video games requiring DirectX 12, advanced Vulkan and recent proprietary manufacturer graphics drivers.
System administrators looking for a system for multi-user production servers with fine-grained access permission management.
Development environments requiring native support for Linux Docker/Kubernetes containers.
content.verdict: Haiku extends the legacy of BeOS. Powered by a hybrid kernel, the BFS file system with indexed metadata and an ergonomic graphical interface, it offers a lightweight alternative for personal computing.

components.name: Haiku kernel
components.note: Kernel written by the project itself; its presentation states that a single team writes the kernel, drivers, userland services, tool kit and graphics stack.

components.name: HaikuDepot
components.note: Central application for software packages: browsing and searching repositories, installing and uninstalling, with featured packages shown by default, as described in the user guide.

components.name: Deskbar
components.note: Desktop panel documented in the Haiku user guide (Deskbar page).

components.name: Tracker
components.note: File and pinboard manager documented in the Haiku user guide.

relations.name: SerenityOS
relations.note: Modern stand-alone operating system designed for personal computing with an integrated C++ desktop graphical interface.

relations.name: ReactOS
relations.note: Open-source reimplementation project of a historical desktop operating system.

relations.name: FreeBSD
relations.note: Free Unix operating system whose hardware drivers and wireless network stack Haiku reuses and adapts.

relations.name: Apple macOS
relations.note: Apple desktop operating system having historically considered the acquisition of BeOS in 1996 before opting for NeXTSTEP as the foundation of macOS.

variants.name: Haiku R1 (R1/beta6)
variants.description: R1 release series; the Get Haiku page lists R1/beta6 as the current version, released on 26 August 2026 for x86 32-bit and 64-bit.
